observedBehavior:
  - "required() and optional() return distinct, unfrozen ordinary objects containing only their kind."
  - "many reads min then max and returns {kind:'many',min,max,order:'profile'} without validating the range."
  - "A read-only direct probe showed many({min:2,max:1}) passes through unchanged, as ADR-0007 requires; the compiler must reject it later."
  - "Optional absence still requires an explicit binding record with an empty provider list; optional does not mean the profile row may be omitted."
  - "No packages/core subject exists at this SHA."
  - "The retained b9 evidence expressly records compilerHandoff as not-executed: research/implementation-readiness/evidence/exact-head-api-probes.json:57-69."
applicability:
  - "Helper behavior applies only to inert declaration authoring; it grants no loading, activation, or lifecycle behavior."
  - "The P1 finding blocks implementation-readiness and public-DX claims, not private exploratory use."
  - "The common-runner mismatch affects only disposable qualification evidence unless someone incorrectly reuses it as compiler or diagnostic authority."
benefits:
  - "Three short, conventional names make cardinality visible at the slot declaration."
  - "many({min,max}) is searchable and avoids positional-argument inversion."
  - "The fixed order:'profile' output prevents registration order from becoming semantics."
  - "Central compiler validation yields one deterministic failure model instead of divergent helper-time checks."
failureModes:
  - "Invalid integers, NaN, negative values, and min greater than max receive no local helper feedback and fail only at compilation."
  - "The word optional may lead maintainers to omit the binding row, although the accepted profile contract requires an explicit empty row."
  - "Mutable helper results can be changed after declaration authoring and before compiler snapshotting."
  - "Lab-only diagnostic names can mislead maintainers evaluating error quality or writing assertions."
counterexamples:
  - "many({min:4,max:2}) is accepted by the helper but must become schema.invalid-value; the accepted vector proves this at architecture/qualification/v1/resource-boundary-vectors.json:108-111."
  - "A required slot with two distinct providers violates required=1 and belongs to binding.cardinality; the common corpus instead expects binding.ambiguous at tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/corpus.ts:51."
  - "A duplicate provider must use binding.duplicate under the accepted catalog, while the common corpus expects binding.provider-duplicate at tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/corpus.ts:50."
